text:
Avery Patel: Quick question — we keep getting brief p99 spikes when KV-cache churn coincides with continuous-batcher coalescing. Curious whether we should move from fixed lease slots to a credit/token-bucket admission tied to kv-cache pressure. Thoughts? :thinking:

Ravi Menon: I like credits for smoothing bursts, but main worry is oscillation between allow/deny causing more churn in the cache.

Chen Li: Can we make the token refill rate a function of kv_cache_hit_ratio and inflight_batches? e.g. slower refill when hit_ratio drops.

Priya Sharma: Agree with Chen. Also add a small guaranteed headroom per-tenant so tiny requests don't starve during global slowdowns. Headroom can be reclaimed if global util < 70%.

Marta Gomez: Observability nit — we currently don't have a single metric that correlates batch size, kv miss-rate, and p99. We need that before we tune refill policies. Otherwise we'll be guessing.

Ken Park: Proposal: hybrid model. Keep lease slots for deterministic fast-path (low-latency tiny requests) and a global token-bucket for larger/coalesced batches. Token bucket adaptively decays tokens when kv_miss_rate > 5%. Sketch config below:

```
admission:
  mode: hybrid
  lease_slots_per_gpu: 6
  token_bucket:
    base_refill_qps: 120
    max_burst_tokens: 300
    decay_factor_on_kv_miss: 0.5   # multiply refill_qps by this when miss_rate high
    min_refill_qps: 20
```

Ken Park: With this we get the tiny-request fastpath and still limit big coalesced bursts when cache pressure spikes.

Ravi Menon: How does eviction work? If tokens are exhausted we should prefer preemptible eviction of the oldest coalesced batch instead of killing lease slot fastpath. That keeps small requests healthy.

Chen Li: +1. Also add a cheap probe per tenant: before allowing a big coalesced batch, sample 1/50 requests to check kv warmness. If probe misses > threshold we delay by a small jitter.

Marta Gomez: For telemetry I can add a derived metric: batch_kv_miss_correlation = cov(batch_size, kv_miss_rate) / var(batch_size). It should surface which tenants/batches drive cache churn.

Priya Sharma: Policy edge-case: what if a noisy tenant keeps borrowing global tokens and never warms cache? We need per-tenant debt accounting + a soft cap. After debt > X, degrade to a throttled steady-state.

Avery Patel: Sounds reasonable. Questions: 1) How invasive is hybrid to runtime? 2) What safety knobs do we need for rollout?

Ken Park: Changes mostly in admission layer + a tiny hook into runtime eviction. We can gate behind a feature flag and do canary on one shard. Add two safety knobs: global emergency kill switch (reject token-bucket grants) and max-burst-per-tenant.

Ravi Menon: For rollout metrics track: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_cache_hit_ratio, inflight_batches, batch_success_rate, and token_borrow_rate_by_tenant. Also watch tail error rates.

deploy-bot: config-change queued: admission.hybrid.enable=true, rollout=canary(shard-7), owner=@Ken Park. 

Avery Patel: Plan: Ken + Chen prototype hybrid in staging on shard-7 for 2 weeks. Marta will add the derived metric before we enable decay_factor. Priya will draft the per-tenant debt/soft-cap behavior. Ravi to define SLO guardrails. If staging looks stable we can run a 48h production canary with emergency rollback. :rocket:

Ken Park: I'll open an RFC follow-up with config proposals, telemetry dashboards, and a short simulation script that models kv_miss-rate feedback.

Chen Li: I'll add the probe sampler and a small unit test harness that simulates cache warm/cold cycles.

Marta Gomez: I'll schedule a quick dashboard sync and add alerts for batch_kv_miss_correlation > 0.2 and token_borrow_rate spikes.

Avery Patel: sweet — thanks everyone. Keeping this thread for follow-ups.
